One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):

Optimums helping Hand Final Script

Commentary One
Every day Optimum mine feeds its coal across a conveyer belt into Hendrina power station. In December the mine was bought by Tegeta Exploration and Resources. Its majority shareholders are the Gupta’s, and Duduzane Zuma, the president’s son has a substantial stake in the business

LINK
This is a story of documents and secret sources, because when you say Gupta’s, Eskom and
coal in the same sentence you get very few insiders prepared to go on camera.

Commentary Two
Its not surprising because in December South Africa realized just how powerful the Guptas had become. Journalists exposed how the Guptas have the power to hire and fire cabinet ministers. And the subsequent allegations that they have captured the state have refused
to go away. In this context the deal was of particular interest to journalists like Phillip De Wet.

Phillip De Wet Associate Editor Mail & Guardian
Effectively the minister of minerals has been responsible for allowing this deal to go ahead. He serves at the sole pleasure of the president whose son is a major beneficiary of the deal the conflict is clear definitely – no one has been able to find a breach of any law or regulation but it doesn’t look good!

Commentary Three
And it didn’t make much sense either. Optimum mine, once made men rich. But by late last year its owners Glencore were losing millions every month. They were locked into a coal supply contract with Eskom till 2018 and at R150 per tonne of coal, they didn’t even cover costs and put the mine into business rescue. In December Tegeta announced the purchase

LINK
To get their hands on Optimum mine they had to get R2.1 billion rand. Once they got the money they would then settle the debt with the bank. But R2.1 billion is a lot of money, even if you are a Gupta

Commentary Four
On the face of it, Eskom weren’t giving the company any special favours. Eskom said they would still have to pay the additional R2 billion rand fine, incurred by Glencore for supplying coal that Eskom said had damaged its power station. Matshela Koko is Eskom’s group executive for Generation

Devi
What is the status of the R2 billion penalty?

Matshela Koko Group Executive Generation
It stands, we want it, its our money!

Commentary Five
On top that Eskom would still buy coal from Optimum mine at the loss making price of R150 per tonne until 2018.

Devi
The Guptas are astute business men would they have invested in a dud?

Phillip laughs
This is of course the question. If you look at this deal as an outsider it doesn’t make sense for that exact reason – The Gupta family has made a lot of money in this country and say what you will about state capture they are good business people, so they must know something that someone else does not know. The numbers just don’t stack up and more importantly the funders behind this cannot be stupid. We do not believe that the Gupta’s and DUDUZANE had between them R2.15 billion in cash to put up

Commentary Six
From the 1st of January Tegeta assumed responsibility for financing Optimum, but they still hadn’t found the money to pay for it. That came later. Now Optimum mine is buzzing, but twenty kilometres away at the Exxaro mine that feeds ARNOT power station, that mine is dead.

LINK
That is the Exxaro mine behind me and for years that mine delivered coal to the Arnot power station. It was really quite simple they mined the coal, slapped it on a conveyer belt and it went straight into the power station. But then the coal began to run out, it became more and more expensive and the only way to reduce the costs was for the mine to expand. Eskom refused and in December last year they had to shut shop

Commentary Seven
Exxaro was shocked, but wont speak out against Eskom, because their other mines depend on them. So we asked Matshela Koko why they shut the mine

Matshela Koko
Because we have been a cash cow, because they have been milking us. Cost plus mines have been milking Eskom!

Commentary eight
Cost plus mines once formed the basis of Eskom’s coal supply. Eskom invested in the mines and in return got good quality coal at low prices. But that model no longer works says Eskom

Matshela Koko
All that I know as ESKOM is that I need R38 billion to capitalize the cost plus mines and I can’t afford it, I don’t have it!




Commentary Nine
But the effect of Eskom’s sudden closure of Exxaro in December left Arnot power station critically short of coal, even though there are still 70 million tonnes of mineable coal

LINK
When our sources handed us this document – they made a shocking allegation- they claimed that Eskom had created an artificially created coal shortfall at Arnot that would enable the Gupta owned Optimum coal to provide coal to ARNOT at inflated prices

Commentary Ten
It was hard to believe that ESKOM would really put the country’s electricity supply at risk to enable the Guptas to make a quick buck, and yet it was clear from this document signed by Matshela Koko, that Tegeta had been given an initial R 586million rand to fulfill Arnot’s emergency order. Umsimbithi, a Glencore company was also contracted to supply Arnot with 540 000 tonnes. Neither went through a tender

Devi
South Africa wants to know if electricity is more expensive, because you are making loaded decisions?
Matshela
No we are moving away from suppliers that milk ESKOM

Commentary eleven
This week Carte Blanche flew over the Optimum mine and captured hundreds of trucks filling up thousands of tonnes of coal and trucking it up the road to ARNOT.

Up sound camera

Suddenly in December Deon Kleynhans who farms cattle and maize right next door to Arnot couldn’t even get into his farm

Deon
Every day is a fight I cant get into farm – coal trucks right in front of my gate ….I also have a business to run …. Cant use the public road anymore …..accident who will be responsible …from a farmers point of view I cant farm next to them anymore they make it impossible

Commentary Twelve
There have been fatalities and the roads are disintegrating. Now the water Deon’s cattle must drink is black from the coal dust. Some of his maize is half the height it should be. But when he approached Eskom they insulted him.

Deon
They make promises then one day they came back and said they don’t speak to uneducated people

Commentary thirteen
He is now taking legal action against Eskom

Devi
So how much of Optimums coal is going to Arnot?
Matshela Koko
Two hundred and fifty- five thousand tonnes up to April.

Commentary fourteen
And yes you guessed it- this coal is of the most expensive that Eskom buys at a fixed cost.

Matshela Koko
R581 delivered

Commentary fifteen
We asked a coal expert to comment on the price.

Coal Expert
The price is incredibly high because they are paying more than R20 per gigajoule which is about twice as much as the normal coal gets sold to Eskom

Devi
So couldn’t you have negotiated a better deal?
Matshela
I will negotiate hard but ultimately I get what I get, but if I can get the coal cheaper elsewhere, I will go there

LINK
Eskom knew that they needed coal for Arnot, as far back as August last year, they put out the tender docs to their regular suppliers, but ten months later those same suppliers are waiting for the tender to be awarded

Commentary Sixteen
And they cannot understand that while they wait ten months for a tender that Eskom wanted them to start supplying on the 1st of January, Tegeta who didn’t tender, are merrily filling up Arnot’s power station at a far higher price than necessary

Devi
Does it take so long?
It does
Why because some of the mines are new but we need to do extensive tests …absorb some of the people at Exxaro

Commentary Seventeen
When the Exxaro mine closed – around 1000 people lost their jobs. NUM’S Mxolisi Hoboyi is perplexed by the closure, not only because of the job losses but because Eskom will have to pay the mine closure costs too

Hoboyi
That is taxpayers money! I am not in business, but it is a very stupid decision to pay about R2 billion rands and you are going to get 0 tonnes. It makes no sense to me

Devi
It looks on the face of it that ESKOM created a path for OPTIMUM mine under the leadership of the Guptas?
Matshela
That is not true, we did not appoint the Gupta’s they were brought to us by the Business rescue practitioners
Devi
But there were other miners who say they had coal available in the area but they were all sidestepped?
Matshela Koko
No …lets start again. We didn’t create a path for anybody. We have proposals of miners that want to supply coal and they are no where any better
Devi
Are you sick and tired of answering questions about the Gupta’s
Matshela
I get sick and tired of people wanting us to treat them differently, because they are not different, because the assumption is that they cannot put an honest tender and win it. when I see an honest tender and win it

Commentary eighteen
But, say several sources they didn’t have to, because Eskom just gave them the contract. Eskom defends their decision and says they got very favourable terms with their two suppliers and they needed to keep the lights on.

Matshela
I have 3000 MW at Arnot. I need to keep the light on, I need coal!

LINK PRE PAYMENT
The big question is how did the Guptas pay for the mine –but this document reveals that perhaps they got a helping hand from Eskom – just a few days before they had to pay the banks Eskom prepaid them at least half a billion rands

PHILLIP
A pre payment is a very interesting thing in this context- somewhere R2.15 billion came from– if you as a GUPTA family walk into a bank with a document from ESKOM promising a prepayment of R800 million rand that is something that it is very easy to loan money against …so if you need R2.15 billion in a hurry and you have an IOU from ESKOM r that helps close the gap very quickly

Devi
Why did Eskom pre pay Optimum half a billion rand for coal
Matshela Koko
We haven’t. We haven’t
You haven’t?
Koko
We haven’t
Devi
Is it common
Koko
We do it yes …there must be a business case and if there is a business case we do it
Devi
But you didn’t pay OPTIMUM any pre payment?
Motshela
I am not aware of that

Commentary nineteen
But the document signed by him authorizes the Chief Financial officer to approve the basis for prepayment for the amount of R586 million 787 thousand rand to Tegeta

Devi
Ok just help me out here this is a document that I have according to this Tegeta has requested some form of prepayment, so what is this?

Koko
You see All the cost plus mines are prepayment, and that is not a surprise to me

Commentary twenty
Our expert disagrees. He says Eskom co invests in the mines and THAT is not the same as prepayment. In a cost plus mine Eskom are not paying for coal they are paying for the mine.

Devi
So did you prepay?
Matshela Koko
I suspect that is the case
Devi
Ya but Mr Koko you said no!
I suspect that is the case let me read it
Devi
Have a look but when I asked you you said no …I asked twice.
Matshela Koko
I am not aware that it is paid, but in the event that it is paid it is not unusual
Devi
No Mr Koko we are not moving on from this as quickly as you would like me to move on
Matshela Koko
Lets say I made a mistake
Devi
Not lets say – you made a mistake!


DEVI
You see one of the biggest mysteries has been how did the Guptas pay the R2.15 billion for Optimum – and now the allegation is this is how they were able to do it, because this is as good as the money in the bank

Matshela Koko
I can’t respond to that That is your version. Here is my version I have a need for coal and I have to secure the quality – in the same way I do with all other mines …when I use the R38 billion rand that is what it is – I pre pay to secure the coal that I need its not unusual

Commentary twenty
But this contract with Tegeta is not a cost plus arrangement.

Coal expert
I have been told that Eskom has never ever paid for coal beforehand so this happening now I don’t understand why
Devi
So arrangement to pay Tegeta is very unusual
Coal Expert
Very

Commentary twenty-one
In this letter sent after our interview he justified the prepayment to Optimum on the basis that they could only supply the right quality for ARNOT by diverting their export quality coal. Optimum needed additional equipment to fulfill delivery to Arnot. Eskom add that the prepayment also included a 3% discount

Phillip De Wet
If ESKOM is being managed in such a way to advantage one company one family then we are in potentially very deep waters indeed – that could undermine the entire system. If ESKOM is not doing everything it can to stretch its rand as far as it can go then you and I should be concerned – this is a company that not only belongs to us it is a company that underpins our entire economy – we probably should give this greater scrutiny than we do any other organization in this country.

Commentary Twenty- Two
Eskom have now extended Tegeta’s so called emergency arrangement until September. They say that these transactions have enabled Eskom to commit to no load shedding during winter. Who knew that we would have the Guptas to thank for keeping the lights on.

THE END 16 min 06 seconds






PROMO ONE 10 seconds
Eskom rejects an allegation that they have given special treatment to Tegeta Exploration and resources when they gave Optimum Mine an emergency contract to supply coal

PROMO TWO 15 seconds
Eskom justifies a pre payment they made to Tegeta for coal to Arnot
Devi
So did you prepay?
Matshela Koko
I suspect that is the case
Devi
Ya but Mr Koko you said no!

PROMO THREE 15 seconds
Is Eskom paying an inflated price for coal to a company linked to the Gupta’s.

Devi
South Africans want to know are they paying more for electricity because you are making loaded decisions
No. no

We haven’t You haven’t? Koko We haven’t Devi Is it common Koko We do it yes …there must be a business case and if there is a business case we do it Devi But you didn’t pay OPTIMUM any pre payment? Motshela I am not aware of that Commentary nineteen But the document signed by him authorizes the Chief Financial officer to approve the basis for prepayment for the amount of R586 million 787 thousand rand to Tegeta Devi Ok just help me out here this is a document that I have according to this Tegeta has requested some form of prepayment, so what is this? Koko You see All the cost plus mines are prepayment, and that is not a surprise to me Commentary twenty Our expert disagrees. He says Eskom co invests in the mines and THAT is not the same as prepayment. In a cost plus mine Eskom are not paying for coal they are paying for the mine. Devi So did you prepay? Matshela Koko I suspect that is the case Devi Ya but Mr Koko you said no! I suspect that is the case let me read it Devi Have a look but when I asked you you said no …I asked twice. Matshela Koko I am not aware that it is paid, but in the event that it is paid it is not unusual Devi No Mr Koko we are not moving on from this as quickly as you would like me to move on Matshela Koko Lets say I made a mistake Devi Not lets say – you made a mistake! DEVI You see one of the biggest mysteries has been how did the Guptas pay the R2.15 billion for Optimum – and now the allegation is this is how they were able to do it, because this is as good as the money in the bank Matshela Koko I can’t respond to that That is your version. Here is my version I have a need for coal and I have to secure the quality – in the same way I do with all other mines …when I use the R38 billion rand that is what it is – I pre pay to secure the coal that I need its not unusual Commentary twenty But this contract with Tegeta is not a cost plus arrangement. Coal expert I have been told that Eskom has never ever paid for coal beforehand so this happening now I don’t understand why Devi So arrangement to pay Tegeta is very unusual Coal Expert Very Commentary twenty-one In this letter sent after our interview he justified the prepayment to Optimum on the basis that they could only supply the right quality for ARNOT by diverting their export quality coal. Optimum needed additional equipment to fulfill delivery to Arnot. Eskom add that the prepayment also included a 3% discount Phillip De Wet If ESKOM is being managed in such a way to advantage one company one family then we are in potentially very deep waters indeed – that could undermine the entire system. If ESKOM is not doing everything it can to stretch its rand as far as it can go then you and I should be concerned – this is a company that not only belongs to us it is a company that underpins our entire economy – we probably should give this greater scrutiny than we do any other organization in this country. Commentary Twenty- Two Eskom have now extended Tegeta’s so called emergency arrangement until September. They say that these transactions have enabled Eskom to commit to no load shedding during winter. Who knew that we would have the Guptas to thank for keeping the lights on. THE END 16 min 06 seconds PROMO ONE 10 seconds Eskom rejects an allegation that they have given special treatment to Tegeta Exploration and resources when they gave Optimum Mine an emergency contract to supply coal PROMO TWO 15 seconds Eskom justifies a pre payment they made to Tegeta for coal to Arnot Devi So did you prepay? Matshela Koko I suspect that is the case Devi Ya but Mr Koko you said no! PROMO THREE 15 seconds Is Eskom paying an inflated price for coal to a company linked to the Gupta’s.
